items.title: fix(oauth-provider): leave request bodies alone when the page query is unsigned

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body: Closes #12072 The `oauth-provider-signin` hook re-serialized every POST body whenever the page had any query string. With no `sig`/`ba_param`, `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returns undefined, but the body had already gone through `safeJSONParse` and `JSON.stringify`, so ISO date strings came back as `Date` output and form bodies were sent as JSON under a form content type. Now the hook returns early when there is no signed query. On a signed page, form bodies stay form encoded with `oauth_query` appended, and JSON bodies are parsed with plain `JSON.parse` so date strings are not rewritten. Tests cover unsigned pages (JSON and form bodies sent byte-identical) and signed pages (form encoding kept, dates unchanged, `oauth_query` added). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #12072 by stopping `oauthProviderClient` from rewriting request bodies when the page query isn't a signed OAuth query. Previously, any query string caused the hook to parse and re-serialize the body even when `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returned undefined, converting ISO date strings to `Date` output and sending form bodies as JSON under a form content type. The hook now returns early when there is no signed query. On signed pages, bodies also keep their original encoding: form bodies stay form-encoded and date strings are left as written while `oauth_query` is added, and JSON parse failures are logged. Tests cover byte-identical JSON and form bodies on unsigned pages and `oauth_query` still being added on signed pages. Written for commit 707b2eda905d195f66f7c61b535f465b9c214ded. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: feat(oauth-popup): accept additionalParams like signIn.social
items.body: ## Summary Closes #12119 `signIn.social` accepts `additionalParams`, but `signIn.popup` had no equivalent, so request-dependent parameters such as `ui_locales` could not be passed to the provider. This adds the option to `signIn.popup`, with the same validation as `/sign-in/social`. ## Changes - `signIn.popup` accepts `additionalParams?: Record` and sends it to `/oauth-popup/start` as a JSON query param (same transport as `additionalData`). - `/oauth-popup/start` validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys such as `state`, `redirect_uri` and PKCE params are rejected) and passes the result to `createAuthorizationURL`. - Invalid params are relayed to the opener as an `invalid_additional_params` completion error, consistent with the other start-stage failures, so the opener does not wait for a timeout. - Changeset added (`minor`). ## Security consideration `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply, unlike the POST `/sign-in/social`. This means a link to the start endpoint can now influence provider-specific authorization parameters (e.g. `login_hint`, `prompt`, `hd`). The impact looks limited: the completion message is only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`, and a start link could already be used to begin a flow without params. I followed the approach proposed in the issue (plain pass-through with the shared schema). If maintainers prefer something stricter, such as an allowlist option on `oauthPopup()`, I'm happy to rework it. ## Testing - Server: params are forwarded to the provider authorization URL; a reserved key (`state`) is rejected; a non-string value is rejected. - Client: params are serialized into the start URL and omitted when unset. - `pnpm vitest run src/plugins/oauth-popup` passes (20 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` passes. There are no docs for `signIn.popup` under `docs/content`, so none were updated; the option is documented via JSDoc. --- ## Summary by cubic `signIn.popup` now accepts `additionalParams` so request-dependent provider parameters like `ui_locales` can be passed, matching `signIn.social` (closes #12119). - The popup client serializes `additionalParams` into the `/oauth-popup/start` URL as a JSON query param, omitted when unset. - The server validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys like `state` and `redirect_uri` rejected) and forwards the result to `createAuthorizationURL`; invalid params return an `invalid_additional_params` completion error instead of leaving the opener waiting for a timeout. ISO-8601 values stay strings rather than being coerced to dates. **Security consideration** - `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply; a start link can now influence provider params like `login_hint` or `prompt`, but the completion message is still only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`. **Testing** - Server tests cover forwarding, reserved-key rejection, non-string rejection, and ISO-8601 string preservation; client tests cover serialization and omission when unset. Written for commit 232cfe6b6838cbfbe9aadb79d09a17e154dbda83. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): skip POST rewrite when OAuth query unsigned

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body: ## Summary `oauthProviderClient()`'s `oauth-provider-signin` `onRequest` hook was re-serializing every non-GET/DELETE body whenever `window.location.search` was non-empty — even when there was no signed OAuth query (`sig` + `ba_param`). Parsing with `safeJSONParse` revived ISO-8601 strings into `Date`s, so `JSON.stringify` corrupted date-like fields (added/truncated ms), turned form-urlencoded bodies into JSON objects, and could turn array bodies into objects. Reset-password pages with `?token=` were a real-world footgun. **Fix:** - Return early before any body parse/re-serialize when `buildSignedOAuthQuery(window.location.search)` is empty. - On the signed-query merge path, parse JSON bodies with plain `JSON.parse` instead of `safeJSONParse` so other fields are not date-revived. Fixes #12072 ## Test plan - [x] Added `packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts` covering: - unsigned query leaves JSON (incl. ISO dates), form-urlencoded, and array bodies untouched - empty / missing search leaves bodies untouched - GET/DELETE skip rewrite even with a signed query - signed query merges `oauth_query` while preserving ISO date strings - existing `oauth_query` is left alone - [x] Local: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts packages/oauth-provider/src/signed-query.test.ts` → 15 passed - [ ] CI green on this PR --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the OAuth provider sign-in hook rewriting POST/PUT/PATCH bodies whenever the page had a query string, even when it wasn't a signed OAuth query. Unsigned query strings like `?token=` used to re-serialize bodies via `safeJSONParse`, which corrupted ISO-8601 date strings (added/truncated milliseconds), turned form-urlencoded bodies into JSON objects, and could turn arrays into objects. The hook now returns early when the window has no search or `buildSignedOAuthQuery` finds no signed query, and uses plain `JSON.parse` when merging the signed query so date fields stay intact. Fixes #12072. - Added `packages/oauth-provider/src/client.test.ts` covering unsigned, empty, and signed query scenarios, plus GET/DELETE skip behavior. Written for commit 50eaa3433e9e1e619b8f61c9ba6d25c4c17b6c8c. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: Client equality gate never suppresses session updates because isJsonEqual returns false for dates
items.body:
### Is this suited for github?

- [x] Yes, this is suited for github

### Reproduction

The client equality gate never suppresses a session update, so every session refetch re-renders `useSession` consumers.

`isJsonEqual` in `packages/better-auth/src/client/equality.ts` handles primitives, arrays and plain objects, but has no branch for `Date`:

```ts
export function isJsonEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
	if (a === b) return true;
	if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) { /* ... */ }
	if (isPlainObject(a) && isPlainObject(b)) { /* ... */ }
	return false; // any Date lands here
}
```

A `Date` is not an array, and `isPlainObject` rejects it because its prototype is `Date.prototype`, so two equal dates fall through to `false`.

That matters because the client parser revives ISO strings into `Date` instances (`parseDates` defaults to `true` in `client/parser.ts`), so the session payload always holds dates.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Sign in and fetch the session twice without changing anything:
   ```ts
   const a = await client.getSession({ fetchOptions: { headers } });
   const b = await client.getSession({ fetchOptions: { headers } });

   a.data.session.expiresAt instanceof Date; // true
   isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data);              // false
   ```
2. `isSessionAtomEqual` calls `isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data)`, so it returns `false`.
3. `withEquality(session, isSessionAtomEqual)` therefore never calls `abort()`, and the `set()` goes through.

Observed on a real instance: `expiresAt instanceof Date` is `true` and `isJsonEqual` on two identical fetches returns `false`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

Two identical session responses compare as different. The equality gate added in #8760 never aborts a `set()`, so every session refetch notifies subscribers and re-renders every `useSession` consumer, even when nothing changed. This is the exact re-render suppression the gate exists to provide.

There is no `Date` coverage in `equality.test.ts`, so this was not a deliberate exclusion.

**Expected behavior**

Two session payloads holding the same instants should compare equal, so the gate aborts the redundant `set()` and no re-render happens.

### What version of Better Auth are you using?

1.6.29

### System info

```bash
Better Auth: better-auth 1.6.29
Affected: packages/better-auth/src/client/equality.ts
Consumers: client/session-atom.ts (isSessionAtomEqual), client/query.ts
Runtime: any (framework agnostic client)
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Client

### Auth config (if applicable)

```typescript
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";

export const authClient = createAuthClient();
// any useSession() consumer re-renders on every refetch
```

### Additional context

`isJsonEqual` is named for JSON values, but the values it actually receives on the client have already been through the date-reviving parser, so dates are always present in practice. Comparing dates by instant keeps the function consistent with the data its only two callers pass it.

items.title: Date fields are not guaranteed to be Date objects at call sites (systemic adapter date-coercion gap)

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

items.body:
## Summary

Throughout the codebase, code that reads a `date`-typed field (`session.createdAt`, `verification.expiresAt`, `key.expiresAt`, and so on) and then constructs a `Date` from it, calls `.getTime()`, or compares it against the current time assumes the adapter returned a real `Date`. That is not guaranteed. Depending on the adapter, the driver, and the storage path, the same field can arrive as a `Date`, an ISO string, a **numeric string** (`"1774295570569"`), or a **number**.

When the value is a numeric string, the `Date` constructor produces `Invalid Date` and downstream arithmetic becomes `NaN`. When it is a plain string, relational comparisons (`field < new Date()`) silently evaluate to `false`. Either way the failure is silent.

This was surfaced by one call site in the `max_age` work (#9936), but it is a data-layer gap, not local to that plugin. There is already a trail of piecemeal fixes for the same root cause (#7937, #3704, #8104, #8105) and open issues touching adjacent facets (#8619, #8882).

## Root cause

The only central coercion is the adapter factory's read transform, and it leaks three ways:

1. It runs only when `supportsDates === false`, but the default is `true` ([factory.ts#L67](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/core/src/db/adapter/factory.ts#L67)), so Prisma, MongoDB, Memory, and Kysely/postgres|mysql trust the driver's return type with no coercion at all.
2. It matches only `typeof value === "string"` and uses a bare `Date` constructor ([factory.ts#L361-L365](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/core/src/db/adapter/factory.ts#L361-L365)), so a `number` is never coerced and a numeric string becomes `Invalid Date`.
3. Secondary storage and the cookie session cache serialize to JSON and never run the adapter transform on read, so dates come back as strings or numbers.

There is no canonical date-normalization in `@better-auth/core`. Instead there are several private reinventions: `normalizeTimestampValue` and `resolveSessionAuthTime` in oauth-provider ([utils/index.ts#L71](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/oauth-provider/src/utils/index.ts#L71), [#L111](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/oauth-provider/src/utils/index.ts#L111)), `deserializeApiKey` in api-key, `toDate` in cimd, and scattered `new Date(...)` wrapping.

This also corrects the premise of #8619, which assumes the runtime "works correctly" by wrapping values in `new Date()`. It does not, for numeric strings.

## Reachability (calibrated)

Default setups are mostly safe: Prisma/Postgres/Mongo return `Date`; the sqlite path coerces ISO strings; `findSession` re-hydrates session expiry; verification entries self-evict via a store TTL. The gap bites with:

- Adapters or drivers that return dates as numeric strings or numbers (better-sqlite3 INTEGER columns, mysql2 with `dateStrings`, custom adapters).
- A few secondary-storage read paths that do not re-hydrate every field (`session.createdAt`/`updatedAt`).

So this is primarily a robustness and adapter-compatibility gap, with a few security-adjacent edges that only activate under those adapters. A maintainer should decide whether any of those edges warrants separate handling; on its own it does not look advisory-grade, because the worst path (verification-token expiry) is mitigated by the store TTL described below.

## Affected call sites

Security-adjacent (wrong security semantics when the date is a string or number):

- OIDC `max_age` and `auth_time`: [oidc-provider/authorize.ts#L308](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/oidc-provider/authorize.ts#L308), [#L331](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/oidc-provider/authorize.ts#L331), [oidc-provider/index.ts#L1063](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/oidc-provider/index.ts#L1063)
- MCP `auth_time`: [mcp/authorize.ts#L208](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/mcp/authorize.ts#L208), [mcp/index.ts#L759](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/mcp/index.ts#L759)
- Fresh-session gate for privileged operations (delete account, change email): [session.ts#L643](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/api/routes/session.ts#L643)
- Session expiry comparison: [session.ts#L370](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/api/routes/session.ts#L370) (and the multi-session and OIDC token-expiry paths)

Correctness and crashes:

- JWKS key handling calls `.getTime()` directly and would throw for a string: [jwt/adapter.ts#L25](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/jwt/adapter.ts#L25), [jwt/index.ts#L192](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/plugins/jwt/index.ts#L192)
- Session field reshaping wraps with a bare `Date`: [internal-adapter.ts#L465](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts#L465), [session.ts#L258](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/api/routes/session.ts#L258)

For contrast, the correct pattern already exists in one place: `consumeVerificationValue` hydrates via `hydrateCachedVerification` ([internal-adapter.ts#L1265](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts#L1265)), while its sibling `findVerificationValue` returns the raw JSON ([internal-adapter.ts#L1147](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/af572166a26c4c84574ce70f6e850a21a6608d70/packages/better-auth/src/db/internal-adapter.ts#L1147)). The expiry checks on the `findVerificationValue` path (2FA OTP, password reset) would fail open for a string expiry, but the secondary-storage entry self-evicts at its store TTL, so this is not exploitable by default; it only bites a primary DB adapter that returns numeric-string dates.

The oauth-provider plugin already defends its own `max_age`/`auth_time` via `normalizeTimestampValue`. The older oidc-provider and MCP sites above do not.

## Proposed fix

Make the data-layer boundary the single source of truth so call sites can trust a `Date`:

1. Promote `normalizeTimestampValue` into `@better-auth/core` on a stable path (e.g. `@better-auth/core/utils/date`). It already handles `Date`, number, numeric string, and ISO string, and returns `undefined` for genuinely unparseable input.
2. In the factory read transform, coerce **every** `date`-typed field through it, regardless of `supportsDates` (replace the gated bare `new Date(...)`).
3. Re-hydrate dates on the secondary-storage and cookie read paths through the same helper, and update the drizzle `customTransformOutput` similarly.
4. Retire the private reinventions and the scattered `new Date()` wrapping.

This changes the adapter contract to always return a `Date` for `date` fields, which is breaking for any third-party adapter that relied on string pass-through, so it targets `next` with a migration note. It also makes the typing question in #8619 answerable: date fields are `Date`, period.

## Related

- #8619 (types don't reflect `supportsDates`; assumes the runtime is already correct)
- #8882 (drizzle + sqlite INSERT flags, the write path)
- #8618, #3704, #7937, #8104, #8105 (earlier piecemeal coercion fixes)

items.title: fix(client): compare dates by instant in the session equality gate

labels.name: core
labels.description: Core infra, API routes, session, cookies, client SDK

items.body: ## Summary `isJsonEqual` had no `Date` branch, so two equal dates fell through to `false`. The client parser revives ISO strings into `Date` instances, so the session payload compared by the equality gate always holds dates. Two identical session responses therefore compared as different, `withEquality` never called `abort()`, and every session refetch re-rendered `useSession` consumers. Closes #10950 ## Why it happens A `Date` is not an array, and `isPlainObject` rejects it because its prototype is `Date.prototype`, so it reached the final `return false`. The gate is wired up in two places, both of which pass parsed payloads: - `client/session-atom.ts`: `isSessionAtomEqual` calls `isJsonEqual(a.data, b.data)`, then `withEquality(session, isSessionAtomEqual)` - `client/query.ts`: `withEquality(value, isAuthQueryStateEqual)` Measured on a real instance before the fix: ``` expiresAt instanceof Date: true two identical getSession() fetches, isJsonEqual -> false ``` and after: ``` two identical getSession() fetches, isJsonEqual -> true ``` ## The fix ```diff if (a === b) return true; + if (a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date) { + return ( + a instanceof Date && + b instanceof Date && + Object.is(a.getTime(), b.getTime()) + ); + } + if (Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b)) { ``` Checking `a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date` first means a date is never mistaken for a plain object, and a date compared against a non-date is correctly unequal. `Object.is` is used so two invalid dates (`NaN`) stay equal rather than reporting a change on every set, which would reintroduce the same loop for malformed values. The JSDoc now records that dates are compared by instant, and why. ## Tests Four tests added to the existing `isJsonEqual` suite: equal instants, different instants, session-shaped data holding dates, and a date compared against a non-date. The two positive tests fail on the unpatched code with `expected false to be true`, which is the bug. Full `equality.test.ts` is 21/21 and the whole `client/` suite is 119/119. `pnpm typecheck` reports no new errors. The 8 pre-existing `schemaName` errors in `packages/cli/test/generate.test.ts` are present on a clean `main` as well and are unrelated. ## Risk Behaviour only becomes more permissive: payloads that were previously reported as changed on every fetch can now be recognised as unchanged. No API or type change. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the client equality gate so identical session payloads containing dates no longer re-render. Previously `isJsonEqual` returned false for `Date` values, so the gate never aborted updates and every session refetch re-rendered consumers. **Bug Fixes** - Detect dates via the `[object Date]` brand and extract the instant with `Date.prototype.getTime.call`, so dates from other realms compare correctly. - Compare `getTime()` with `Object.is` so two invalid dates are equal and avoid update thrash. - Add tests for cross-realm dates, spoofed `Date` tags, equal/different instants, session-shaped payloads, nested dates in arrays, and date vs non-date. - No API or type changes. Written for commit 9c723476194cd3d356b43e7825285a0ba88e82b5. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(drizzle-adapter): support dates in string columns

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

labels.name: locked
labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

labels.name: devops
labels.description: CI/CD, GitHub Actions, build tooling, e2e tests, release automation

items.body: ## Summary A Drizzle schema that stores dates in string columns broke every Better Auth write. Drizzle passes the value of `timestamp({ mode: "string" })`, MySQL `datetime({ mode: "string" })` and SQLite `text()` to the driver unchanged, and in Drizzle 0.45 those columns have no driver mapping, so the adapter's `Date` reached the driver: | Driver | On `main` | |---|---| | postgres-js | `TypeError: The "string" argument must be of type string ... Received an instance of Date` | | better-sqlite3 | `SQLite3 can only bind numbers, strings, bigints, buffers, and null` | | Cloudflare D1 | `D1_TYPE_ERROR: Type 'object' not supported` (#10816) | Email sign-up returned 422 `FAILED_TO_CREATE_USER`, and filters on those columns, such as `expiresAt > now` when listing sessions, failed the same way. The Drizzle 1.0 relations adapter has the same problem for SQLite `text()`. A second bug sat behind the first. A string without a time zone, as PostgreSQL `timestamp` and MySQL `datetime` return, was read with `new Date(value)`, which parses it as the server's local time. On a server outside UTC, every date read back shifted by the UTC offset. ## Fix `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/date-columns.ts` holds two helpers, used by both the 0.x and the relations v2 adapters: - `toDriverDate`, called from `customTransformInput`, so it covers create, update, updateMany, `incrementOne` `set`, and where values. When a `Date` is bound for a column whose Drizzle `dataType` is a string type (`"string"` in 0.x, `"string ..."` in 1.x), it writes UTC text: ISO 8601, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm` for MySQL, which is what Drizzle's own MySQL date mode writes. Date-mode columns are untouched. - `fromDriverDate`, called from `customTransformOutput`, reads a date-time without an offset as UTC, as Drizzle's date mode does, and otherwise behaves like `new Date(value)`. The relations v2 adapter had no output transform, so string columns came back as strings there. Detection is per column, so a schema that mixes `text()` and `integer({ mode: "timestamp_ms" })` dates works without a new option. Setting `supportsDates: false` would not work either: it makes the factory send strings to date-mode columns as well, and those call `toISOString()` on whatever they receive. ## Compatibility Schemas generated by the CLI use date-mode columns and see no change. One setup changes behavior: node-postgres or mysql2 with a string column that has no time zone, on a server whose time zone is not UTC. Those drivers accepted a `Date` and wrote it in local time, so existing rows now read back shifted by the server's offset. The changeset says so. ## Tests The e2e tests call the adapter directly on one `user` table and run in `America/Los_Angeles`, so reading a value without a time zone is checked off UTC. - `e2e/adapter/test/drizzle-adapter/adapter.drizzle.string-dates.test.ts` writes, filters on, updates and reads back a `Date` on PostgreSQL via postgres-js (`timestamp({ mode: "string" })`) and SQLite via better-sqlite3 (`text()`). It also checks the stored text. Both tests fail on `main`. With only the write fix, the PostgreSQL test still fails. - `e2e/adapter/test/drizzle-v2-relations-adapter/adapter.drizzle.string-dates.test.ts` does the same for SQLite `text()` on Drizzle 1.0 rc.3, plus a stored value without a time zone. It fails on `main`, and the time-zone case fails with only the write fix. - `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/date-columns.test.ts` covers what the e2e tests can't reach: Drizzle 1.x data type names, the MySQL format, `Date` lists for `in`/`not_in`, offsets, microseconds, and date-only strings. - MySQL `datetime({ mode: "string" })` with mysql2 passed an earlier sign-up version of the e2e test locally. It isn't committed, because the MySQL adapter suite drops and recreates the shared `better_auth` database while other files run. - The full Drizzle 0.45 (1387 tests) and relations v2 (1419 tests) e2e suites pass. `postgres` (already in the lockfile through `e2e/integration/vanilla-node`) is added to the e2e adapter workspace for the postgres-js case. Closes #7419 Closes #10816 Closes #9498 replaced: the write coercion here also covers where values, `incrementOne`, relations v2, Drizzle 1.x data types and UTC reads; thanks @ping-maxwell, credited as co-author Closes #10898 replaced: per-column detection handles mixed `text()` and integer date columns without a new `supportsDates` option --- ## Summary by cubic Drizzle adapters now write dates in string-backed columns as UTC text and read timezone-free values as UTC, preventing driver errors and timezone shifts on writes, where clauses, and `in` / `not_in` filters, plus reads on the relations v2 adapter. **Compatibility** - Existing rows written in server-local time with node-postgres or mysql2 may read back shifted by the server's UTC offset; CLI-generated date columns are unaffected. **Tests** - E2e tests run in `America/Los_Angeles` against PostgreSQL via postgres-js and SQLite via better-sqlite3, covering `timestamp({ mode: "string" })` and `text()` writes, filters, updates, and reads; the relations v2 suite also verifies reading a timezone-free value as UTC. - The unit test covers Drizzle 1.x data types, the MySQL format, Date lists in `in` / `not_in`, explicit offsets, microseconds, and date-only strings. items.body: Add an opt-in `userSchemaExtensions` option to the SCIM plugin. Declared extensions are advertised through /Schemas and the User ResourceType, validated on ingress, stored, round-tripped in responses, and support schema-qualified PATCH (add/replace/remove). Each attribute may optionally be mapped to a `user.additionalFields` key so it is queryable outside SCIM. Only simple singular attributes are supported (string, boolean, integer, decimal, dateTime, reference); complex and multi-valued attributes are out of scope. Custom extensions are lenient about schema declaration — a present extension value auto-declares its URN — for interoperability with providers such as Microsoft Entra, while the Enterprise extension keeps its strict contract. Startup validation checks that each mapped field exists, is optional, and is type-compatible, and warns when a mapped field is end-user writable. The static User schema graph is refactored into builder factories fed per instance, keeping the existing constants as zero-extension defaults so behavior is unchanged when no extensions are declared. Closes #10980 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in `userSchemaExtensions` option to the SCIM plugin so applications can carry custom User attributes through provisioning. Declared extensions are advertised through `/Schemas` and the User ResourceType, validated on ingress, stored, round-tripped in responses, and support schema-qualified PATCH; each attribute can optionally map to a `user.additionalFields` key to be queryable outside SCIM. **Scope** - Only simple singular attributes are supported (string, boolean, integer, decimal, dateTime, reference); `dateTime` values must be real RFC 3339 dates and map to a `Date` on the user field. Complex and multi-valued attributes are out of scope. - Custom extensions auto-declare their URN when an extension value is present, so providers such as Microsoft Entra can omit the declaration; the Enterprise extension keeps its strict contract. - Startup validates that each mapped field exists, is optional, and is type-compatible, and warns when a mapped field is end-user writable. Case-variant attribute names are canonicalized on ingress, and `returned: "never"` attributes are stripped from responses. - PATCH matches the longest URN prefix and validates root fragments per attribute; a pathless op merges and a `null` value clears only the targeted attribute, while `replace` on the extension root replaces and clears omitted attributes. - Per-attribute selection via `attributes`/`excludedAttributes` is not yet supported for custom extension attributes; full-resource GET still returns them. **Refactors** - The static User schema graph is now built per instance via builder factories; existing constants remain zero-extension defaults, so behavior is unchanged when no extensions are declared. Closes #10980 Written for commit cf3a4c2410109a502d27751cd868001b787f648b. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: Add supportsDates option to allow string as timestampz from db

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: locked
labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

items.body:
Better Auth currently looks only at the database type to decide if it should handle timestams as Date or string.
This PR extends this feature to allow customizing this behavior:

```ts
    // Force timestamp-like types to be returned as raw strings
    // to preserve full precision for downstream consumers
    types: {
      // PostgreSQL OIDs for timestamp-related types
      timestamptz: { from: [1184], to: 1184, parse: (s: string) => s, serialize: (s: string) => s },
      timestamp: { from: [1114], to: 1114, parse: (s: string) => s, serialize: (s: string) => s },
      date: { from: [1082], to: 1082, parse: (s: string) => s, serialize: (s: string) => s },
      time: { from: [1083], to: 1083, parse: (s: string) => s, serialize: (s: string) => s },
      timetz: { from: [1266], to: 1266, parse: (s: string) => s, serialize: (s: string) => s },
    },

    // later on I init betterAuth:
  export const auth = betterAuth({
  // Use Better Auth's Kysely adapter with supportsDates: false for Neon compatibility
  // This prevents crashes when the database driver returns dates as strings
  database: kyselyAdapter(db, {
    type: 'postgres',
    supportsDates: false, // NEW: Fix for Neon/PostgreSQL driver returning dates as strings
  }),
```

Without that, I get `ERROR [Better Auth]: Failed to create user TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Date`

Took me quite some time to debug, I used AI to write this fix, so the tests defo need work,
but I wanted to get the discussion going first if this is something you consider.

And since I'm fairly new to web tech, also if this pattern is common.
I did talk with @igalklebanov and he confirmed that this is a common pattern.


Alternative design if we wanna be even more explicit (but then I'd expect auto to do a one-time probe)
```ts
  dates: 'auto',           // default
  // dates: 'native',     // force Date passthrough
  // dates: 'string',     // force ISO strings at DB boundary
```

Why go in on all strings?
This allows my project to keep full precision on time and greatly simplify date/time conversion.
Everything is a zod-verified timestamp, date conversion happens at the UI layer.
Especially with React RSC that's super nice, so I can push my existing models to the frontend.

Why not read from the db layer?
I considered reading the config from the database but that gets messy fast - I use Neon in prod which again has a differert type configuration syntax - so a new option seemed easier.

No conversion?
I use `postgres.js` which returns [correct ISO 8601](https://github.com/porsager/postgres/blob/32feb259a3c9abffab761bd1758b3168d9e0cebc/src/types.js#L31), as does Neon. pg returns ISO (with a space instead of T + numeric offset) so folks using that still have to do a tiny conversion or a [json_object trick](https://onecompiler.com/postgresql/43v4ab5kn) to get ISO 8601.
    
<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---

## Summary by cubic
Adds a supportsDates option to the Kysely adapter to control how date/time fields are handled. This prevents crashes with drivers that return strings (e.g., Neon Postgres) and allows preserving full timestamp precision by using ISO strings.

- **New Features**
  - New config: supportsDates. When false, dates are handled as strings. Defaults remain: sqlite/mssql=false, postgres/mysql=true. Can be overridden per adapter.
  - Added tests to cover defaults and overrides.

- **Migration**
  - If your Postgres driver returns dates as strings (e.g., Neon), set supportsDates: false in kyselyAdapter({ type: 'postgres', supportsDates: false }).

<!-- End of auto-generated description by cubic. -->
